title: Horse series: Aristides, winner of the first Kentucky Derby
summary: Bred at McGrathiana near Lexington, the little chestnut Aristides was entered as a pacesetter and won the first Kentucky Derby on May 17, 1875, for trainer Ansel Williamson and jockey Oliver Lewis.
bodyMarkdown:
Nobody expected Aristides to win the first Kentucky Derby. He was supposed to set the pace for a better horse.

## A small colt at McGrathiana

Aristides was [foaled in 1872 on McGrathiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristides_%28horse%29), the Fayette County farm of H. Price McGrath. McGrath had been born poor in Jessamine County, went west in the Gold Rush, and opened a gambling house in New York; the story goes that a single night’s winnings of $105,000 paid for his return to Kentucky and his stud farm. The colt was by the English stallion Leamington, and his dam, Sarong, was a daughter of [Lexington](/stories/lexington-blind-hero-of-woodburn/). McGrath named him for his friend Aristides Welch of Pennsylvania, who had imported Leamington.

He was a chestnut with a white star and two white hind stockings, foaled late and small, never much over 15 hands. He went down in Derby lore as [“the little red horse.”](https://history.ky.gov/markers/aristides) McGrath did not think him first-rate. His stablemate Chesapeake was the one the farm counted on.

## Two horses, one plan

The Louisville Jockey Club, organized in 1874 by [Meriwether Lewis Clark Jr.](https://history.ky.gov/markers/churchill-downs-2), modeled its new race on England’s Epsom Derby. On [May 17, 1875](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1875_Kentucky_Derby), about 10,000 people came out to the track, not yet called [Churchill Downs](https://grokipedia.com/page/Churchill_Downs), to watch fifteen three-year-olds run a mile and a half. Thirteen of the fifteen jockeys were African American.

McGrath ran both colts in his green and orange silks. The plan was simple. Aristides would break fast and run the field into the ground, and Chesapeake would come from behind to win. Aristides was ridden by [Oliver Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Lewis), a 19-year-old born free in Versailles in 1856, and trained by [Ansel Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansel_Williamson), who had been born enslaved in Virginia around 1806 and had conditioned champions such as Asteroid for Robert A. Alexander of Woodburn.

The first part worked. Aristides went to the front, gave up the lead briefly, then took it back and kept widening it. The second part did not. Chesapeake broke badly and never threatened.

In the stretch Lewis looked toward McGrath for orders, and [McGrath waved him on](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristides_%28horse%29). Aristides held off Volcano and won by about two lengths in 2:37¾, a record for the distance in America.

## After the Derby

Lewis and Aristides were second in the Belmont Stakes that summer. Lewis never rode in another Derby; he left the saddle after that season and later worked as a bookmaker in Lexington before moving to Cincinnati. Williamson won the Belmont that same year with Calvin and was elected to the National Museum of Racing’s Hall of Fame in 1998.

Aristides won nine of 21 starts, was sold after McGrath died in 1881, and died in St. Louis on June 21, 1893. He was voted into the Hall of Fame in 2024.

## Kentucky today

A [KHS marker for Aristides](https://history.ky.gov/markers/aristides) stands by the Legacy Trail on what was McGrathiana, now part of the University of Kentucky’s Coldstream Research Campus. At Churchill Downs, where the pin sits, a life-size bronze of the little red horse stands in the Clubhouse Gardens.
